body.estimand_functional: \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\tau_R)=(\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B,\ q^\top\{\widehat s_1-\widehat y(\widehat M)_r^+\widehat B\})\), with root-\(K\) influence \((\Phi_{\theta},\Phi_\tau)\)

sampling_model.design: A fixed set of target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and target factual-post cells is observed; treatment histories and grid times are fixed.
sampling_model.units: Each cell contains \(K\) independent individuals, and cell samples are mutually independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The target switches treatment after the pre period while donor units remain under control. For the positive joint theorem, the exact post-transport equality identifies the target's untreated post-period survival row; target-pre row span is not additionally required there.
sampling_model.overlap: Conditional censor survival is at least \(g>0\) through every required cell horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. The general cell theorem assumes \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), origin normalization, bounded variation of \(R_{cf}\), and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). The variation condition is an additional primitive sufficient condition not implied by generic product-rate or machine-learning consistency; Westling et al. instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate. On the separate finite-stratum submodel with positive at-risk masses, hazards bounded away from one, and training size at least a fixed fraction of \(K\), clipped empirical conditional hazards verify the event-ratio and variation rates with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) impose event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, use a fixed-grid latent-factor/PCR transport, and form the spectral inputs from marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves; they do not derive covariate-adjusted AIPCW spectral influence inference.
Published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) gives asymptotic linearity for a directly estimated cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

body.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, rank, and a separated nonzero singular spectrum, covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates have a joint root-\(K\) expansion conditional on explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation-rate restrictions on fitted event-survival paths. A clipped empirical discrete-hazard learner verifies those restrictions at rate \(K^{-1/2}\) on a finite-stratum submodel with positive at-risk probabilities and hazards bounded away from one; this certificate does not validate generic learners or the TCL application. Differentiating the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post blocks yields a joint Gaussian law that may be singular. Nonzero counterfactual marginal variances suffice for the simultaneous band, and a separate nonzero grid-RMST variance suffices for scalar studentization. Post-transport alone supplies the causal equality for the joint theorem; target-pre span remains relevant only to the Han--Shah embedding and the converse subclass. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains open.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) already state event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but their spectral workflow uses marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and does not give a covariate-adjusted joint influence law. With heterogeneous covariates, conditional independence need not imply marginal independence, so those cell inputs can converge to distorted curves before PCR transport. Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) provide asymptotic-linearity theory for a directly estimated treatment-specific curve, not for a learned three-block spectral counterfactual.
project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage and the transported counterfactual is a smooth spectral functional on a separated-rank neighborhood. The bridge requires the exact Stieltjes remainder under a disclosed learner-path variation restriction, all three terms of the pseudoinverse derivative, and only statistic-specific nondegeneracy for inference.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the conditional AIPCW cell expansion and supplies a finite-stratum clipped empirical-hazard certificate attaining its event-side conditions at root-\(K\) rate. It then proves the possibly singular joint transported Gaussian law with consistent covariance estimation; after the two atomic variance premises are installed, the simultaneous band and grid-RMST interval use only their respective marginal and scalar variances. The project also retains the open-subclass Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias result and leaves the weak-gap frontier open.

body.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but use marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and do not derive a covariate-adjusted transported influence law. The present joint theorem uses exact post-transport as its causal equality and does not additionally use target-pre row span; that span remains in the separate Han--Shah embedding and Kaplan--Meier/PCR converse subclass. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4) and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply the cross-fitted augmented survival-score architecture and direct-curve inference, not learned spectral transport. The relative-survival variation restriction here is an additional primitive sufficient condition not imposed by Westling et al., who instead assume the exact Stieltjes-remainder rate; the finite-stratum proposition proves one attainable empirical-hazard submodel rather than a generic learner theorem. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) study minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) are the matrix-calculus ancestor for the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but not this three-block PCR pseudo-limit. Fan and Liao (2022) study growing-panel factor models, while Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) study robustness to rank misspecification. These are neighboring problems; weak-gap and selected-rank inference for the unregularized fixed-donor pseudoinverse target remains an acknowledged open frontier of this note.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional. Its general cell layer is conditional on bounded variation and the stated \(L_2\) variation rate for fitted relative-survival paths; ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) survival-ratio consistency does not imply that restriction. The empirical-hazard certificate covers only fixed finite covariate and event-time supports with uniformly positive observed at-risk probabilities, event hazards bounded away from one, and training folds of order \(K\); it is not a generic machine-learning result and is not asserted for the TCL application. The joint Gaussian covariance may be singular. Bands exclude zero-variance counterfactual coordinates, and the grid-RMST interval separately excludes a zero scalar variance. The theory does not cover growing grids or panel dimensions, shrinking singular gaps, selected rank, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST.
body.honest_scope: The joint cell and spectral results cover a fixed-panel, fixed-grid, exact-rank, fixed-singular-gap, exact-post-transport class. They additionally require within-cell i.i.d. sampling, cross-cell independence, conditional independent censoring, censor positivity, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, event-origin normalization, and the primitive bounded-variation and relative-variation-rate restrictions on the event learner. Target-pre row span is not required by the joint spectral limit; it remains only in the Han--Shah embedding and the Kaplan--Meier/PCR converse subclass. Full positive definiteness of \(\Omega_\eta\) is not required: the joint theorem allows a singular Gaussian law, while the band needs only positive counterfactual coordinate variances and the grid-RMST interval needs only its scalar influence variance. The finite-stratum certificate verifies the event-side learner restrictions only when covariates and event times have fixed finite support, observed at-risk masses are uniformly positive, event hazards are bounded away from one, and every training complement has size at least a fixed fraction of \(K\). It does not establish those properties, cross-cell independence, or the other sampling conditions for the 925-patient TCL application. Nothing here covers growing dimensions, a shrinking or closed singular gap, selected rank, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains the acknowledged follow-on open frontier.
